notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 run ros-wave-c-110; driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null. No human reviewed or tested anything, no hardware was attached, and no ROS graph, Gazebo world, state plugin, object recognizer or simulator run is claimed. The clone at 0bd506d52c7e0a1791a0488afab5c31fc34e2347 was not modified.

SELECTED DEVICE AND SCOPE: the package serves the source-backed Gazebo object-state sensor. It binds the object_msgs/ObjectInfo service on the absolute /gazebo_objects/get_info (gazebo-pkgs-noetic/gazebo_state_plugins/config/GazeboObjectInfo.yaml:12; type include gazebo-pkgs-noetic/gazebo_state_plugins/include/gazebo_state_plugins/GazeboObjectInfo.h:9) and the object_msgs/Object topic on /gazebo_objects (config/GazeboObjectInfo.yaml:8; type include GazeboObjectInfo.h:8). The service is the primary observation because the shipped config sets publish_world_objects false (GazeboObjectInfo.yaml:4); the topic is an explicit observation that may be silent unless the operator enables the state plugin publisher or runs the upstream FakeObjectRecognizer (gazebo-pkgs-noetic/gazebo_test_tools/config/FakeObjectRecognizer.yaml:3,7; launch/gazebo_fake_object_recognition.launch:6-14). The plugin creates the /gazebo_state_plugins node handle and advertises the service unconditionally (src/GazeboObjectInfo.cpp:32,56); its callback returns success=false with OBJECT_NOT_FOUND for a missing model and otherwise success=true, NO_ERROR and the object from createBoundingBoxObject (src/GazeboObjectInfo.cpp:59-75). The package fixes get_geometry=false, so the service returns pose fields only (general-message-pkgs-master/object_msgs/srv/ObjectInfo.srv:1-23); it carries the object name, frame and object.origin pose (the first collision pose, src/GazeboObjectInfo.cpp:177-250).

NOT COVERED: the arm and hand MoveIt/ros_control motion is not bound. The clone declares arm_controller and hand_controller as position_controllers/JointTrajectoryController (lora_moveit_config/config/ros_controllers.yaml:1-2,41-42) and names them in simple_moveit_controllers.yaml with action_ns follow_joint_trajectory and plugin type FollowJointTrajectory (:2-4,13-15), but it never declares the fully qualified ROS action type, the resolved action endpoint or an acknowledged stop. demo.py:13-14 is a MoveGroupCommander client, not a server provided by this repository. The package therefore makes no arm/hand motion or robot-arm safety claim; this is an object-state sensor, not a motion driver. Also NOT COVERED: the object_msgs/Object primitive, mesh and plane geometry arrays (the real primitive_poses array has one pose per collision of the requested model; the package carries only object.origin, the first collision pose), the grasp fix plugin, contact handling, the map publisher, TF, Gazebo physics, cameras and depth sensors. The world's 0.001 s maximum physics step and 1000 Hz real-time update rate (inspire_hand_description/worlds/demo_world.world:72-76) are source facts, not the deployed fake's timing.

SAFETY: the device is simulated R0. The package has no actuation commands, so there is no native stop to reach; the runtime latches in software, refuses further extension observations, and no motion is commanded. The x-cap read actions remain latched even with verb read. The fake and the gate evidence are contract_checked only; no hardware backend, hardware review or hardware test is claimed. The card requires publish_review because the upstream licence is NOASSERTION; the package must not be published before the owner's decision.

FIDELITY AND LIMITS: the deployed fake is an event-driven ROS-free recording transport at F0: no Gazebo physics, object dynamics, controller, recognizer, wall-clock pacing or state-hash replay. Its object names and poses are placeholders (# placeholder in fake.py), not facts; a live run must receive them from the operator's Gazebo world and the pinned GazeboObjectInfo plugin. No numeric input exists, so no Limit is declared and the G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE warning is expected; there are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. fixtures/conformance.json supplies the two placeholder object names for the read probes.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked both bindings (the absolute /gazebo_objects/get_info service and /gazebo_objects topic from the shipped GazeboObjectInfo.yaml, the object_msgs types from the plugin header, the request, success predicate and result paths against ObjectInfo.srv and Object.msg), the ROS 1 header shape of the fake, all 25 facts and the observation-only R0 scope against the vendored gazebo-pkgs, object_msgs, the MoveIt config and the README at the pin. Defects: the createBoundingBoxObject fact and the notes said origin is the first collision pose, but origin_init is never set to true (GazeboObjectInfo.cpp:189-227), so origin is the world pose of the model's last collision element; nine facts said more than their lines (a publisher topic name and a service type off their lines, origin-mode constants outside Object.msg:1-47, the recognizer topic's message type off line 7, 'loads the state plugins' for a launch that loads parameters, and interpretive clauses on the two controller facts and demo.py), and the controller facts said the clone declares no action endpoint although simple_moveit_controllers.yaml names action_ns and the short type; the package did not disclose that the README demo (demo_gazebo.launch, gazebo.launch) starts Gazebo without the libgazebo_world_plugin_loader.so system plugin and loads no gazebo_state_plugins parameters, so neither endpoint exists there, that FakeObjectRecognizer republishes only objects a client registered through /gazebo_test_tools/recognize_object, or the vendored licence conflicts. The reviewer corrected the docstring, ten facts, the three pose-field descriptions and the topic gap, and added twelve source facts (publisher behaviour, the recognizer timer, plugin_loader.launch, WorldPlugins.yaml, the system-plugin loader, the README run steps, gazebo.launch, the four licence statements) and two gaps (driver.py), updated facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass; the stable digest is unchanged (sha256:249ca8d35ccec056f35b4f9fbb0d9d36899bb518d17ee2f7ad62ddafd3d93b88), and the author's notes on a first-collision origin, on the topic's sources and on an undeclared action endpoint are superseded. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Observation only (no actuation, no stop needed): the object-info service and topic come from the vendored gazebo-pkgs world plugin, which the repository's own README demo does not load; a deployment must start gzserver with -s libgazebo_world_plugin_loader.so and load plugin_loader.launch parameters before Gazebo starts. The reported x, y, z are the world pose of the model's last collision element, and a model without collisions is answered success true with a zero origin. The arm and hand (MoveIt FollowJointTrajectory controllers) are not covered. Licences: no root licence (NOASSERTION); the vendored gazebo-pkgs-noetic and general-message-pkgs-master carry BSD 3-Clause LICENSE files while gazebo_state_plugins/package.xml says GPLv3 and object_msgs/package.xml says LPGv3; publish_review required, the owner decides.
